quote: Where natural regeneration is an option to restore a degraded mangrove area, and availability of propagules and seeds is ensured, restoration planning should first examine and validate the potential existence of primary stresses such as blocked tidal inundation that might prevent nat- ural succession from occurring, and remove those stressors to enhance natural recovery. This can be achieved through hydrological restoration, that is re-modification and re-establishment of original conditions of the ecosystem including tidal regimes (Turner and Lewis 1996; Kamali and Hashim 2011). Where signs of natural recov- ery are not observed within 6 to 12 months after adjustments of the physical conditions, consid- eration for undertaking actual mangrove refor- estation either through direct planting of propagules collected from the forest or nursery- raised seedlings should be considered and evalu- ated (see also Chapter 6).

context.practice_as_described: mangrove restoration; hydrological rehabilitation, natural regeneration and planting distinguished
context.numeric_calibration: No numerical suitability function, cutoff, score or runtime weight established.
context.note: Natural-recruitment pathway requires propagule/seed supply and removal of stresses including disrupted tidal flow. If no recovery after the stated 6–12 months, evaluate planting; this is a monitoring decision interval, not a suitability threshold. Better regeneration reduces need for planting, but does not reduce whole-family suitability. Hydrological rehabilitation attribution retained.

quote: It is important to clarify land ownership for the restoration site from the beginning of the project because unclear land tenure can hinder success of a restoration project, threatening the long-term conservation of the site and project investment. This problem can be avoided by making clearly understood written long-term agreements with the landowners and users to ensure they are all committed to the project.

quote: La teneur en eau du sol et la qualité physico- chimique des eaux interstitielles sont contrôlés par la texture du substrat. L'étude granulométrique sur les trois fractions suivantes (sable, silts et argile, sur des échantillons de sol prélevés à différentes profondeurs au niveau des 20 à 30 premiers centimètres) est donc capitale pour l'analyse des facteurs d'échecs ou de succès dans un projet de restauration de mangrove. (English: Soil water content and the physicochemical quality of porewater are controlled by substrate texture. Grain-size analysis of sand, silt and clay in soil samples from different depths within the upper 20 to 30 centimetres is therefore crucial for analysing failure or success factors in a mangrove restoration project.)

quote: Dans le cas où existe une forêt de mangrove en bon état de santé et une bonne disponibilité de propagules, adjacente à la zone de restauration, on considère qu'il suffit de procéder à la réhabilitation hydrologique pour rétablir la mangrove. Cela induira une colonisation naturelle, sans qu'il soit nécessaire de procéder à un reboisement, sachant que le rétablissement de la couverture naturelle sera plus lent. (English: Where a healthy mangrove forest with good propagule availability adjoins the restoration area, hydrological rehabilitation is considered sufficient to restore mangroves through natural colonisation without replanting, although recovery of natural cover will be slower.)
